Patient demographics:

  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married

  pcl5: 65

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Intrusive Thoughts: Unwanted thoughts, Visual (Injuries): Visible injuries or wounds on others, Authority Presence: Police
  Maladaptive Strategies: Screen Escape: I spend long hours on my phone, games, or internet to avoid thinking, Avoid People: avoid other people, Mental Distraction: keep mind occupied all the time
  Threat: Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place, Escape Route Planning: I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere, Body on Alert: My body feels constantly tense and ready to react to danger
  Memory: Overwhelm on Recall: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop, Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning, Cannot Explain Clearly: When I try to explain what happened I lose the thread and cannot finish
  Negative Appraisals: Lost Meaning: Nothing in my life feels meaningful anymore, Life Destroyed: My life has been destroyed by the trauma, Injustice: What happened to me was deeply unfair and nothing has been done about it

Vignette:
Michael, a 46-year-old graphic designer, had always found comfort in the routine of his life. Married for over twenty years, he shared a home with his supportive wife, Rachel, in a quaint suburb. They enjoyed quiet evenings filled with laughter, the two of them often sharing their thoughts over dinner while the sunlight painted the walls in warm hues. However, beneath this seemingly serene surface lay the remnants of a trauma that had irrevocably altered his existence.

The trauma struck one evening in the heart of a bustling downtown area. Michael had been walking home from a local café, enjoying a rare moment of solitude. Suddenly, the sound of sirens pierced the air, and chaos unfolded before him. He witnessed a police officer tackle a young man to the ground, shouting commands as the man struggled. In that moment, Michael felt a visceral connection to the scene — the visible injuries on the young man, the desperate pleas for help, and the overwhelming sense of injustice. The officer's presence felt like a dark cloud, suffocating the air around him. It was as if time had stopped, and he found himself frozen in place, helpless and terrified.

Since that fateful night, Michael's life had spiraled into a series of increasingly isolating behaviors. He could hardly step outside without scanning the environment for police cars or officers. The very sight of someone in uniform sent his heart racing. He had come to believe that the world was filled with lurking dangers, and he could no longer trust what was around him. Even in safe spaces, like his home, he found himself unable to relax, his body perpetually tense, always ready to flee. He would often plan escape routes in his mind, mapping out exits even in familiar settings, a habit that had begun to seep into his work life. At the office, he would sit in meetings, his mind preoccupied with potential ways out, rather than focusing on the discussions at hand.

In an effort to cope with the anxiety that had become his constant companion, Michael resorted to maladaptive strategies. He found solace in the glow of his phone screen, spending hours lost in games and social media, avoiding the thoughts that threatened to overwhelm him. Days turned into weeks as he distanced himself from friends and colleagues, isolating himself under the guise of being too busy with work. Each time Rachel suggested a social outing, he would find a reason to decline, fearing that being around others would trigger unwanted memories of that night. 

His mind buzzed with a relentless need for distraction, never allowing a quiet moment to pass. When memories from the traumatic event clawed their way back into his consciousness, they wrapped around him like a vise, squeezing the air from his lungs. He would try to articulate what had happened, but the words eluded him, leaving him feeling more fragmented and disoriented. What frightened him most was the intensity of the emotions that surged forth when he attempted to recall that night; they were overwhelming, driving him to retreat further into his self-imposed isolation.

As the months dragged on, the weight of the trauma became unbearable. Michael felt as if his life had been destroyed, each day blending into the next in a haze of despair. He struggled to find meaning in his work and personal relationships, the joy he once derived from his creative pursuits diminished to a mere flicker. He often voiced to Rachel that nothing felt worthwhile anymore; the world had become a place of darkness, and he was lost within it. The injustice of what he had witnessed gnawed at him relentlessly — why had no one intervened? Why did the system seem so indifferent? These questions haunted him, leaving him feeling powerless and trapped in a cycle of anger and sorrow.

Finally, after months of silent suffering, Michael reached a breaking point. One night, staring blankly at a screen filled with notifications he could no longer bear to read, he realized he could not continue living this way. He saw the toll it had taken on his marriage, the cracks in his relationship with Rachel deepening with each passing day. The thought of losing her was unbearable, and it was the catalyst he needed. It was time to seek help, even though he feared the process would unearth emotions he had long buried. What he hoped for most was to reclaim his life, to find a way back to the man he once was, and perhaps, to rediscover the meaning that had eluded him for so long.
